# Discovery: UX/UI Improvement Proposal — Ultron

**Generated by:** Discovery Facilitator persona (Aitri pre-planning)
**Date:** 2026-03-03
**Status:** Ready for Product

---

## 1. Problem Framing

**Current state:** Ultron is a functional Go-based hardware monitoring dashboard (Raspberry Pi) with a dark theme, HTMX, SSE streaming, and a sidebar-navigated multi-page web UI. The dashboard was built iteratively and has accumulated UX debt: metric tiles show limited context (percent only, no absolute values), the settings page is 413 lines and handles multiple concerns in a single scroll, navigation has no current-state feedback on mobile, and the sidebar collapse behavior differs between mobile and desktop.

**Pain:** The admin loses context switching between pages (no breadcrumb, no persistent status bar), cannot quickly assess system health at a glance without reading individual tiles, and has no fast path to critical alerts from any page.

**User:** Single Raspberry Pi owner/operator (Admin) who monitors the device daily, primarily from desktop browser, occasionally from mobile.

**Why now:** Multiple UX-focused features (`ux-ui-upgrade`, `revision-ux-ui`) have already been approved and executed, but no structured UX evaluation has been performed against the actual templates and interaction flow. Further iterations without this baseline risk diminishing returns or contradictory changes.

---

## 2. User and JTBD

**Primary user:** Admin (sole operator)

**Jobs to be done:**
1. *When I open the dashboard,* I want to know immediately if anything needs attention — so I don't have to scan every tile manually.
2. *When I navigate between pages,* I want to know where I am and how to get back — so I don't lose context.
3. *When I'm on mobile,* I want the same core information available without horizontal scrolling or collapsed data.
4. *When an alert fires,* I want to see it from wherever I am in the UI — so I don't miss it.

**Baseline (how it works today):**
- Dashboard shows 5 metric tiles (CPU, RAM, Disk, Network, Temp) with percent values and color states (normal/warning/critical)
- Timeline chips (5m/2h/6h/12h/24h) control chart window — positioned top-right, small text
- Sidebar has 7 items with Lucide icons; collapses on desktop, hides on mobile with hamburger toggle
- Alert badge appears in sidebar nav item only when alerts are active
- Settings page handles backup, Telegram, alerts, hardware, security, and system in one long scroll
- No persistent status bar, no breadcrumb, no global health indicator

---

## 3. Scope Boundaries

**In-Scope:**
- Dashboard tile information density (add absolute values alongside percentages)
- Global alert visibility (persistent indicator accessible from all pages)
- Mobile navigation usability (sidebar show/hide behavior, touch targets)
- Settings page information architecture (tab or section grouping to reduce scroll)
- Timeline chip discoverability and affordance
- Visual hierarchy improvement within existing dark theme tokens

**Out-of-Scope:**
- Technology stack change (Go/HTMX/Tailwind stays)
- New monitoring data sources or metrics
- Authentication flow redesign
- External media assets or CDN dependencies
- Color scheme change (dark theme is a hard constraint)

---

## 4. Constraints and Dependencies

| Constraint | Detail |
|---|---|
| Stack locked | Go + HTMX + Tailwind CSS + SSE — no JS framework |
| Low-resource profile | Raspberry Pi 4/5 — no heavy client-side rendering, no large bundles |
| Dark theme required | Existing CSS token system (`text-accent`, `metric-tile`, etc.) must be preserved |
| No external assets | Per `total-stabilization` spec: only local assets |
| HTMX SSE patterns | Real-time sections (`sse-swap`) limit certain interaction patterns |
| Single-user | No multi-tenant, no role-based UI changes needed |

---

## 5. Success Metrics

**Primary KPI (leading):**
- Time-to-insight on dashboard: Admin can assess system health status in under 5 seconds from page load (measured by: all critical indicators visible above the fold on 1080p desktop and 390px mobile without scroll)

**Guardrails:**
- Page weight does not increase by more than 5% (Tailwind purge must remain active)
- No existing Go handler changes required for Phase 1 improvements (template-only changes)
- All existing tests remain green after template changes

**Lagging indicators:**
- Reduction in settings-related navigation confusion (qualitative, assessed by user after delivery)
- Zero regression in SSE streaming behavior after template refactor

---

## 6. Risk and Assumption Log

| Rank | Risk/Assumption | Confidence | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Settings page grouping may require new route handlers for tabs | Medium | Verify if HTMX tab switching can work with existing single `/settings` route before spec |
| 2 | Mobile sidebar behavior relies on JS toggle logic — changes may break it | Medium | Read `base.html` JS carefully before proposing changes |
| 3 | SSE swap targets are id-bound — adding new elements near swap zones may cause partial-update collisions | High | Keep new elements outside existing `sse-swap` target divs |
| 4 | Assumption: Admin uses desktop browser primarily | Low risk | Single-user product, low cost if wrong |
| 5 | Alert badge already exists in sidebar — extending to global bar is additive, not breaking | High confidence | Confirmed in sidebar.html |

---

## 7. Discovery Confidence

**Confidence:** High

**Reason:** The codebase is fully readable, templates are well-structured, existing token system is consistent, and the scope is bounded to template/CSS changes for Phase 1. No ambiguity in user identity (single admin). Success metric is verifiable (above-fold visibility test).

**Evidence gaps:**
- No user session recording or heatmap data available (single-user product — acceptable)
- Settings page tab feasibility (HTMX route constraint) — needs 1 technical spike before spec locks

**Handoff decision:** `Ready for Product`
